translations.title: Beloved Images of Athens...
translations.text:
Beloved images of Athens.

In the Plaka district,
near Monastiraki,
an ordinary street with many shops.

If anyone who loves me
ever goes to Greece
and passes through there, especially in summer,
let them commend me to it.

It was a Monday in August,
after a terrible year; I had just arrived.
I remember suddenly loving life
because the street smelled
of cooking and shoe leather.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Song for That Day
translations.text:
Here comes the time to release doves
in the middle of statue-filled squares.
Our hour is about to strike. At any moment
the bells will ring.

Look at the tender buds of the trees
becoming visible in the newly opened light.
Light ribbons hang from cloud
to cloud. And garlands

across the breast of the sky, pulsing,
are like the breath of a voice. Words
will soon be spoken. Listen. You can hear
the sound of footsteps and the beating of wings.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: The Night Takes Hold...
translations.text:
The night takes hold
without a breath, like an effort.
More slowly, without a kindly breeze
to stir uncertain weariness for an instant
and hasten sleep's release.
From identical lights
a high wall of windows keeps watch.
Sleepless flesh alone, bodies
lie like severed hands,
lean out, seek the love of the air
—and the ember they draw on lights
eyes where anxiety never sleeps,
the infinite hope with which the night afflicts us
when it returns.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: The Outskirts (II)
translations.text:
Who? Who is sleeping?
If I fall silent, does he breathe?
Someone is there,
asleep on the outskirts.

The outskirts are vast,
sheltered, deep.
I know, but is there no one
who can tell me more?

They are almost within reach,
and darkness falls on the road
without telling us where
we would want to sleep.

The wind passes. Shall I call it?

If it climbed into October's
familiar drawing room,
the gentle silence
would be terrified.

And perhaps I too would be afraid
if it told me, beyond recall,
who sleeps
on the outskirts.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: As It Turns Out
translations.text:
As it turns out, it is possible to declare oneself a man.
As it turns out, it is possible to say no.
At once, in the street, at once, for everyone
and for all the times when we could not.

As it turns out, being alive matters.
As it turns out, even unjust force
needs, depends on our lives, these small acts
everyone performs in the street each day.

And we must not forget the lesson:
know at every moment that the gesture we make
contains a hidden weapon; know that we are
still alive. And that life
is still possible, as it turns out.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: The Outskirts (IV)
translations.text:
You remember. The dawning years,
as peaceful as time, pure childhood
vaguely cared for by the world.

The night still sheltered us like a mother.
We came from sleep, and a warmth,
a taste like the first night,
lingered on our lips,
moistening and softening the day.

But something sometimes called to us.
The body, and summer's return,
the afternoon itself, too vast.

On what morning, do you remember, did we want
to peer into the dangerous well
at the far end of the garden? The still water
endured, like a gaze
in whose depths we saw our image.

And a sudden silence fell
upon the world, startling us.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Now I Wonder Whether All Our Lives...
translations.text:
Now I wonder whether all our lives
we have been here. Just now I put
my hand before my eyes—how the blood
beats in my eyelids—and the enormous
hairs blur silently
before my gaze. My lashes feel heavy.

I do not quite know what I am saying. Who are they,
those vague faces swimming as though in pale water,
seated here, alive with us?
The afternoon drives us to certain bars
or among tired men in pajamas.

Come. Let us go outside. Night. There is space
above, higher, far higher than the lights
that flash across your widened eyes.
There is silence too between us,
silence,

and this kiss like a long tunnel.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Ruins of the Third Reich
translations.text:
Everything happened as he had imagined
back there at the Smolensk front.
And you have aged, though you still smile
wie einst, Lili Marlen.

Haloed in mist, just as before,
your lovely face rises before me
against a background of tanks
and swastikas in the Place Vendôme.

At the bar, before a drink,
planted there like a decoy,
you smile obscenely.
At whom, Lili Marlen?

Defeated by the Russians and by years,
your angry heart still asks
you for war. And in the final hours
of solitude and alcohol,

enraged and thin, you use your nails
to tear the stitching of your black glove,
your old black gauntlet
with which you waved goodbye as you left.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Eyes of a Solitary Boy, Astonished...
translations.text:
Eyes of a solitary boy, astonished,
whom I caught watching us
in that little pine grove near the Faculty of Letters
more than eleven years ago,

as I was about to part,
still dazed by saliva and sand,
after we had rolled together, half dressed,
happy as animals.

I remember you; it is strange
how, with the concentrated force of a symbol,
you are bound to that story,
my first experience of love returned.

Sometimes I wonder what became of you,
and whether now, at night beside a body,
the old scene comes back
and you still spy on our kisses.

Thus from the past returns to me,
like an incoherent cry,
the image of your eyes. An expression
of my own desire.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.
